text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Vietnam and Australian parliamentarians say both their countries will benefit from stability and development in the Asia-Pacific. The comments were made during a visit by Australia's House of Representatives Speaker, Bob Halverson.
-- A Bangladeshi trade delegation led by Minister of Trade and Industry Tofail Ahmed is visiting Vietnam to boost bilateral commercial ties between the two countries.

-- In a letter sent to the president and members of Non-Aligned Movement, President Le Duc Anh said Vietnam would do its utmost for the "notable targets" set by the NAM, which is marking its 35th anniversary.
-- The Vietnam Youth Union is holding a conference on HIV/AIDS to raise awareness about the epidemic in Vietnam and its devestating effect on youth.

-- The Australian House of Representatives' delegation, led by Speaker Bob Halverson, on Monday held discussions with the Chairman of Vietnam's National Assembly, Nong Duc Manh, and Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet.

-- Typhoon Willie hit the coastal provinces of Nghe An and Ha Tinh on Sunday night, causing serious damage. Some 4,000 houses were flooded, 1,500 other houses lost their roofs, 17,350 hectrares of paddy fields were submerged, 15,500 trees were uprooted and dykes and roads were damaged.

-- The Vietnam-Bulgarian inter-govermental committee for economic and technical cooperation held its 16th meeting in Sophia last week. The two sides signed an agreement on investment protection and promotion.
-- 12,000 sodiers and millions of militias joined an anti-flood and natural calamities force.
-- Foreign Minister Nguyen Manh Cam left for the United Nations General Assembly in New York after a three-day official friendship visit to Cuba.
-- Hanoi's Communist Party cell held a conference to review its activities in the last four years.

-- By the end of August the Ministry of Planning and Investment had granted licenses for 193 joint ventures and 100 percent foreign-owned projects. The amount of foreign investment licensed for industrial production and infrastructure was greater than in the same period last year.
-- IBM will finance Vietnam's Youth Soccer Championship '96.
